newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND LEADS AFTER FIRST DOWNHILL RUN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND LEADS AFTER FIRST DOWNHILL RUN.

text.p: Frenchman Luc Alphand prevailed on the slope where he captured his maiden victories two years ago to take the lead after the first leg of a two-run World Cup sprint downhill on Friday.
Alphand, who won two Kitzbuehel downhills staged on the same day in 1995, clocked the quickest time of one minute 6.26 seconds on a shortened version of the dreaded Streif piste.
The 31-year-old defending downhill World Cup champion is looking for a third victory this winter after topping the podium in the Italian resorts of Val Gardena and Bormio in December.
He was closely trailed by Austria's Werner Franz, in 1:06.33, on the 2,020-metres long course which had a vertical drop of 529 metres.
Franz is eager to finish on the rostrum and secure a place in the Austrian downhill team for the world championships in Sestriere in less than two weeks.
Switzerland's Franco Cavegn and Italian Werner Perathoner tied for the third-best first-descent time of 1:06.45 on an overcast day.
Atle Skaardal, who won the first-ever two-run downhill staged here in 1990, was fourth after the first run, with 1:06.56.
